title: Critical current: criteria, geometry and pinning
summary: Compare transport, magnetization and depairing limits with their field, time scale and area convention. Preserve measurement conditions before comparing conductor performance.

claims.statement: Critical current is a limit defined for a specimen, measurement protocol and operating conditions. Transport measurements use a voltage or electric-field criterion; magnetization measurements infer a current through a model; the depairing current describes loss of stability of a superconducting state within a specified theory. These quantities must not share an unlabeled performance ranking.

claims.statement: Blatter and colleagues explicitly distinguish depinning and depairing current densities in their review abstract. Pinning, thermal fluctuations and vortex motion affect practical current transport. A measured threshold can instead be limited by weak connections or heating; its mechanism requires evidence beyond the value of the current itself.
claims.conditions: Qualitative vortex/pinning interpretation; not a fitted universal Jc or critical-field boundary.
claims.verificationScope: Pinned chapter plus Blatter publisher abstract; full review remains unchecked.

claims.statement: A simple sensitivity calculation illustrates why the criterion matters. If a measured interval is modeled by $E=E_0(J/J_0)^n$ with positive constant $n$, changing the criterion by a factor $r$ changes the inferred current by $r^{1/n}$. For $n=20$, a tenfold criterion change gives a factor of about 1.122. This is an illustrative power-law calculation, not a measured exponent or a universal transport law.

claims.statement: The magnetic force density is the vector product $\mathbf F=\mathbf J\times\mathbf B$. For current perpendicular to the induction, its magnitude at the threshold becomes $F_p=J_cB$ if a static pinning-force balance is the applicable model. In SI units this is N/m³; resistive heating instead has power density $\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf J$ in W/m³. A parallel configuration has no force from this cross product. Replacing $B$ by $\mu_0H$ requires an additional approximation, especially near self-field conditions.

claims.statement: Keep enough information to reconstruct both the measured threshold and the conversion to a current density. The following is an editorial reporting guide, not a table of certified material records.

claims.statement:
| Measurement | Record with the result | Interpretation boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Transport | Temperature, field magnitude and orientation, voltage-tap spacing, electric-field criterion, current ramp or pulse duration, duty cycle, area convention | Contact heating, current sharing and voltage offsets can change the inferred threshold |
| Magnetization | Magnetic moment, volume, dimensions, field history, sweep rate, elapsed time and background subtraction | Conversion to current requires a geometry and critical-state model |
| Conductor or cable | Superconducting fraction, whole-conductor area, length, strain and thermal stabilization | Layer current density and engineering current density answer different questions |
| Depairing model | Model, temperature regime, geometry and stability assumptions | A calculated instability is not automatically the measured transport limit |

claims.statement: MacManus-Driscoll and colleagues studied YBCO films grown with BaZrO3 added to the target. Their selected manuscript passages report improved in-field transport at 75.5 K, despite lower transition temperature or self-field current in some samples. The rotated field remained perpendicular to current. This comparison illustrates distinct performance measures, not proof of a different pairing mechanism. No electric-field criterion was extracted here, so no numerical current record is tabulated.

claims.statement: Larbalestier and colleagues' 2014 paper is a primary Bi-2212 round-wire study, not a general engineering review. Its earlier author manuscript distinguishes whole-conductor $J_e$ from superconducting-area $J_c$ and compares short specimens with a demonstration coil. This entry uses that distinction without importing a cross-family ranking; the final published dataset and all measurement criteria were not independently re-extracted.

claims.statement: An irreversible magnetic response and the upper critical field are different observables. A loss of measurable hysteresis or a transport threshold need not locate the destruction of superconductivity. Report the criterion, time scale and field history rather than silently equating an irreversibility line with $H_{c2}$. Thermally activated creep is one reason different observation times can yield different apparent current limits.

claims.statement: A fitted pinning-curve exponent or angular peak does not uniquely identify a defect. Compare microscopy, processing controls and temperature/angle dependence. In the checked YBCO manuscript, the detailed composition of the small second-phase particles is not conclusively established; describing every particle as chemically proven BaZrO3 would overstate the evidence.

claims.statement: Separate a better transport path, stronger pinning, a larger superconducting fraction and a higher depairing limit as distinct hypotheses. Compare controlled specimens under matched conditions before assigning an improvement to a microscopic mechanism. A gain in current-carrying performance does not by itself demonstrate higher $T_c$, a new pairing interaction or a new superconducting phase.
